registers.name_in_paper: longitudinal administrative register data covering the entire Danish population
detailed schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education
matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells

variables_mentioned: annual unemployment duration (fraction of the calendar year insured workers spend unemployed)

registers.name_in_paper: tax-assessed asset values, sickness benefits, area of residence, and marital and cohabitation status
variables_mentioned: sickness and maternity leave benefits received from the municipality
cohort-specific childcare quality and availability at the municipal level

linkages: Every resident has been assigned a unique personal identification number since 1968, which permits linkage across all national registers
children linked to their parents, and parents linked to their employers and tax records
plant records linked to individual job spells to track each plant's owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses
each treated child matched 1:1 without replacement to an untreated child of the same birth year, child gender and displaced-parent gender, defining a placebo closure year for the control

sample.universe: Children aged 0-22 in the year of a real or placebo parental plant closure, born 1986-2002, whose parent is a private-sector employee aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure at the firm
sample.unit_of_observation: child (one observation per child for end-of-school outcomes); child-year for the parental event studies of Equation (3)
selection_rules: restrict to private-sector plants, because distinct workplaces are difficult to identify in the public sector

a plant is classified as closed if several of its characteristics (owner, industry, municipality, workforce) change from one year to the next, unless a large share of employees is re-employed at a single newly established plant

require a minimum reduction of three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce, in plants with at least five employees five years prior to closure; among the last three years of operation the closure year is the year with the largest employment decline (51,002 closures, 1986-2017)
select workers aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure at their firm, applied in t* for exposed workers and in any year for unexposed workers
restrict to workers exposed to exactly one closure
keep children treated by at most one parental closure, i.e. whose mother or father, but not both, experiences a plant closure
restrict to children born by the calendar year of parental job loss
restrict to children born 1986-2002, because educational records span 2002 to 2018

partition into cells by birth year, child gender and displaced parent's gender; within each base year and cell perform 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching without replacement, minimising differences in parental age at childbirth, three-digit industry, plant size, tenure, earnings in t*-1 and t*-2, child's number of siblings and birth order
98% of treated children matched, giving 130,927 treatment-control pairs
sample.period: Plant closures 1986-2017; educational records 2002-2018; employer-employee data 1980-2017
sample.n_observations: 261,854 children in the main matched sample (130,927 treatment-control pairs); analysis samples range from 82,528 to 261,854 depending on outcome and sample split
sample.n_individuals: 133,805 treated children in the working sample across ages 0-22; 130,927 treated children successfully matched

construction_notes: Grades are standardised to have a mean of zero and unit variance within the corresponding subject-year distribution
Earnings and post-tax income are expressed in 2020 Danish kroner (7.46 DKK per euro, 6.54 DKK per US dollar)
Unemployment duration measures the fraction of the calendar year insured workers spend unemployed, normalised to 1000 for a full year
Family post-tax income sums the parents' incomes; for the Table 4 split it is measured two years prior to the real or placebo job loss

Childhood stages: infancy 0-1, early childhood 2-5, middle childhood 6-11, late childhood (adolescence) 12-16; ages 17-22 form the post-school-age reference group; a(i) is the child's age in the closure year t*+1
In Figure 2 the authors construct 80 binary indicators for scoring at or above equally spaced thresholds in the (-2 sd, 2 sd) interval, coding non-participants as zero
Asset values are summed between parents and outlier asset values are winsorized at levels exceeding the 75th percentile by three times the interquartile range (Figure 5)
The number of observations in Table 2 is computed before the exclusion of singleton observations (3 units in column 3)
Teacher assessments are highly correlated with exam scores (0.86 in the paper's sample)

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in infancy (ages 0-1), lowers test taking, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22.

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in infancy (ages 0-1). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 0-1; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to one if the child has at least one recorded grade-nine mark, from either continuous teacher assessment or a formal examination, and zero otherwise. The paper interprets it as a proxy for grade completion; a zero typically indicates grade retention, dropout, or transfer to a non-standard educational track where conventional grading is not applied.

timing.value: Measured at the end of compulsory schooling, grade nine, at age 16.

units.value: proportion of children (0/1 indicator); a coefficient of 0.01 equals one percentage point

magnitude.interpretation: Given a baseline participation rate of 92%, this decline explains approximately 13% of the observed non-completion.

estimand.target_population: Children aged 0-1 in the year their parent's plant closed, whose parent was a private-sector employee aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure
estimand.time_horizon: Outcome measured once, at the end of compulsory schooling (grade nine, age 16); for children exposed in infancy (ages 0-1) this is 15-16 years after the parental job loss.
estimand.formal_query: E[Y | do(parental plant closure at child age in 0-1)] - E[Y | do(no parental plant closure)], for treated children, differenced against the same contrast for children aged 17-22 at closure

population.selection: Children of private-sector employees aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure at their firm; children exposed to at most one parental plant closure (mother or father, not both); children born by the calendar year of the job loss; treated children matched 1:1 without replacement within cells of birth year, child gender and displaced-parent gender (98% matched, 130,927 pairs).

identification.source_of_variation: Plant closures and major downsizings at private-sector plants in Denmark, 1986-2017 (51,002 events), identified from matched employer-employee registers; the child's age in the closure year determines the childhood stage of exposure, and children aged 17-22 at closure (for whom the shock cannot affect end-of-school outcomes) serve as the within-design reference group.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age-invariant selection into treatment: in the absence of treatment, any systematic difference in end-of-school outcomes between treated and matched control children would have remained constant across children treated at different ages.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Nonparametric age-at-closure estimates from Equation (2) (Figure 1) are statistically indistinguishable from zero for job losses after compulsory school age; F-tests for the joint significance of the post-compulsory coefficients fail to reject (p = 0.49 for test-taking, p = 0.92 for mathematics); no systematic trends in mathematics achievement among control children by age at placebo job loss (Online Appendix Figure D.1).

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion for the reference group: parental plant closure occurring after the child has completed compulsory schooling (ages 17-22) cannot affect end-of-school performance, so that group identifies the selection term rather than a treatment effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the design's central insight; Figure 1 shows coefficients for ages 18-22 indistinguishable from zero.

implies_edges.from: Parental plant closure when the child is aged 17-22

formal.as_written: the earliest age at which parental plant closure cannot affect end-of-school outcomes

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: plant closures are difficult to anticipate, so families do not adjust fertility or other pre-closure choices in response to a foreseen closure.
key_assumptions.supported_by: 83% of closures leave the plant with no employees and the median closing plant has the same headcount in the year before closure as in the preceding year; robustness to 'pure' closures, to closures with gradual downsizing, and to excluding children born in the closure year (Online Appendix B).

key_assumptions.assumption: Displaced workers are negatively selected on characteristics unobserved by the matching procedure; the design concedes this latent common cause and assumes only that its influence does not vary with the child's age at exposure.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Hilger (2016) evidence on negative selection into closing plants; baseline imbalances in Online Appendix Table D.1; the estimated beta1 in Table 2 is large relative to the treatment effect.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age-invariant selection into treatment: in the absence of treatment, any systematic difference in end-of-school outcomes between treated and matched control children would have remained constant across children treated at different ages.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Nonparametric age-at-closure estimates from Equation (2) (Figure 1) are statistically indistinguishable from zero for job losses after compulsory school age; F-tests for the joint significance of the post-compulsory coefficients fail to reject (p = 0.49 for test-taking, p = 0.92 for mathematics); no systematic trends in mathematics achievement among control children by age at placebo job loss (Online Appendix Figure D.1).

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion for the reference group: parental plant closure occurring after the child has completed compulsory schooling (ages 17-22) cannot affect end-of-school performance, so that group identifies the selection term rather than a treatment effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the design's central insight; Figure 1 shows coefficients for ages 18-22 indistinguishable from zero.

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16), has no statistically significant effect on test taking, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22.

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 12-16; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to one if the child has at least one recorded grade-nine mark, from either continuous teacher assessment or a formal examination, and zero otherwise. The paper interprets it as a proxy for grade completion; a zero typically indicates grade retention, dropout, or transfer to a non-standard educational track where conventional grading is not applied.

timing.value: Measured at the end of compulsory schooling, grade nine, at age 16.

units.value: proportion of children (0/1 indicator); a coefficient of 0.01 equals one percentage point

estimand.time_horizon: Outcome measured once, at the end of compulsory schooling (grade nine, age 16); for children exposed in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16) this is 0-4 years after the parental job loss.
estimand.formal_query: E[Y | do(parental plant closure at child age in 12-16)] - E[Y | do(no parental plant closure)], for treated children, differenced against the same contrast for children aged 17-22 at closure

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in mid childhood (ages 6-11). key_assumptions.assumption: Age-invariant selection into treatment: in the absence of treatment, any systematic difference in end-of-school outcomes between treated and matched control children would have remained constant across children treated at different ages.

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion for the reference group: parental plant closure occurring after the child has completed compulsory schooling (ages 17-22) cannot affect end-of-school performance, so that group identifies the selection term rather than a treatment effect.

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16), has no statistically significant effect on teacher assessment in maths, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22.

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 12-16; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Standardised grade-nine continuous teacher assessment in mathematics, conditional on the child having a recorded mark. Grades are standardised to mean zero and unit variance within the corresponding subject-year distribution.

timing.value: Measured at the end of compulsory schooling, grade nine, at age 16.

units.value: standard deviations of the grade distribution within the corresponding subject-year

estimand.target_population: Children aged 12-16 in the year their parent's plant closed, whose parent was a private-sector employee aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure

identification.source_of_variation: Plant closures and major downsizings at private-sector plants in Denmark, 1986-2017 (51,002 events), identified from matched employer-employee registers; the child's age in the closure year determines the childhood stage of exposure, and children aged 17-22 at closure (for whom the shock cannot affect end-of-school outcomes) serve as the within-design reference group.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age-invariant selection into treatment: in the absence of treatment, any systematic difference in end-of-school outcomes between treated and matched control children would have remained constant across children treated at different ages.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Nonparametric age-at-closure estimates from Equation (2) (Figure 1) are statistically indistinguishable from zero for job losses after compulsory school age; F-tests for the joint significance of the post-compulsory coefficients fail to reject (p = 0.49 for test-taking, p = 0.92 for mathematics); no systematic trends in mathematics achievement among control children by age at placebo job loss (Online Appendix Figure D.1).

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion for the reference group: parental plant closure occurring after the child has completed compulsory schooling (ages 17-22) cannot affect end-of-school performance, so that group identifies the selection term rather than a treatment effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the design's central insight; Figure 1 shows coefficients for ages 18-22 indistinguishable from zero.

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in infancy (ages 0-1), lowers teacher assessment in maths, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22.

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in infancy (ages 0-1). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 0-1; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Standardised grade-nine continuous teacher assessment in mathematics, conditional on the child having a recorded mark. Grades are standardised to mean zero and unit variance within the corresponding subject-year distribution.

units.value: standard deviations of the grade distribution within the corresponding subject-year

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in infancy (ages 0-1). definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in early childhood (ages 2-5). definition.value: Composite binary index equal to one if, by the end of compulsory school (age 16), the student either recorded multiple educational spells within the same academic year, grade retention, or failure to complete an academic year; realised at least once.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age-invariant selection into treatment: in the absence of treatment, any systematic difference in end-of-school outcomes between treated and matched control children would have remained constant across children treated at different ages.

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion for the reference group: parental plant closure occurring after the child has completed compulsory schooling (ages 17-22) cannot affect end-of-school performance, so that group identifies the selection term rather than a treatment effect.

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in mid childhood (ages 6-11), raises dropout, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22.

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in mid childhood (ages 6-11). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 6-11; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to one if the child is not in education at age 16 or fails to complete the school grade started at that age. The latter completion is not observed for the 2002 birth cohort.

timing.value: Enrolment status at the start of the academic year in which the child is 16.

units.value: proportion of children (0/1 indicator); a coefficient of 0.01 equals one percentage point

estimand.target_population: Children aged 6-11 in the year their parent's plant closed, whose parent was a private-sector employee aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure
estimand.time_horizon: Outcome measured once, at the end of compulsory schooling (grade nine, age 16); for children exposed in mid childhood (ages 6-11) this is 5-10 years after the parental job loss.
estimand.formal_query: E[Y | do(parental plant closure at child age in 6-11)] - E[Y | do(no parental plant closure)], for treated children, differenced against the same contrast for children aged 17-22 at closure

population.description: Matched 1:1 nearest-neighbour treated-control pairs (130,927 pairs) of children aged 0-22 in the year of the real or placebo parental plant closure; completion of the school grade started at age 16 is not observed for the 2002 birth cohort; N = 250,348 for this column.

population.selection: Children of private-sector employees aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure at their firm; children exposed to at most one parental plant closure (mother or father, not both); children born by the calendar year of the job loss; treated children matched 1:1 without replacement within cells of birth year, child gender and displaced-parent gender (98% matched, 130,927 pairs).

identification.source_of_variation: Plant closures and major downsizings at private-sector plants in Denmark, 1986-2017 (51,002 events), identified from matched employer-employee registers; the child's age in the closure year determines the childhood stage of exposure, and children aged 17-22 at closure (for whom the shock cannot affect end-of-school outcomes) serve as the within-design reference group.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age-invariant selection into treatment: in the absence of treatment, any systematic difference in end-of-school outcomes between treated and matched control children would have remained constant across children treated at different ages.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Nonparametric age-at-closure estimates from Equation (2) (Figure 1) are statistically indistinguishable from zero for job losses after compulsory school age; F-tests for the joint significance of the post-compulsory coefficients fail to reject (p = 0.49 for test-taking, p = 0.92 for mathematics); no systematic trends in mathematics achievement among control children by age at placebo job loss (Online Appendix Figure D.1).

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion for the reference group: parental plant closure occurring after the child has completed compulsory schooling (ages 17-22) cannot affect end-of-school performance, so that group identifies the selection term rather than a treatment effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the design's central insight; Figure 1 shows coefficients for ages 18-22 indistinguishable from zero.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in mid childhood (ages 6-11). claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16), has no statistically significant effect on general programme, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22.

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 12-16; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to one if, at age 16, the child is enrolled in a general upper-secondary programme (academically oriented gymnasium or business/technical college).

units.value: proportion of children (0/1 indicator); a coefficient of 0.01 equals one percentage point

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in infancy (ages 0-1), lowers test taking, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (children whose displaced parent is the FATHER).

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in infancy (ages 0-1). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 0-1; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to one if the child has at least one recorded grade-nine mark, from either continuous teacher assessment or a formal examination, and zero otherwise. The paper interprets it as a proxy for grade completion; a zero typically indicates grade retention, dropout, or transfer to a non-standard educational track where conventional grading is not applied.

units.value: proportion of children (0/1 indicator); a coefficient of 0.01 equals one percentage point

identification.source_of_variation: Plant closures and major downsizings at private-sector plants in Denmark, 1986-2017 (51,002 events), identified from matched employer-employee registers; the child's age in the closure year determines the childhood stage of exposure, and children aged 17-22 at closure (for whom the shock cannot affect end-of-school outcomes) serve as the within-design reference group.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age-invariant selection into treatment: in the absence of treatment, any systematic difference in end-of-school outcomes between treated and matched control children would have remained constant across children treated at different ages.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Nonparametric age-at-closure estimates from Equation (2) (Figure 1) are statistically indistinguishable from zero for job losses after compulsory school age; F-tests for the joint significance of the post-compulsory coefficients fail to reject (p = 0.49 for test-taking, p = 0.92 for mathematics); no systematic trends in mathematics achievement among control children by age at placebo job loss (Online Appendix Figure D.1).

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion for the reference group: parental plant closure occurring after the child has completed compulsory schooling (ages 17-22) cannot affect end-of-school performance, so that group identifies the selection term rather than a treatment effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the design's central insight; Figure 1 shows coefficients for ages 18-22 indistinguishable from zero.

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in early childhood (ages 2-5), has no statistically significant effect on test taking, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (DAUGHTERS).

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in early childhood (ages 2-5). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 2-5; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to one if the child has at least one recorded grade-nine mark, from either continuous teacher assessment or a formal examination, and zero otherwise. The paper interprets it as a proxy for grade completion; a zero typically indicates grade retention, dropout, or transfer to a non-standard educational track where conventional grading is not applied.

timing.value: Measured at the end of compulsory schooling, grade nine, at age 16.

units.value: proportion of children (0/1 indicator); a coefficient of 0.01 equals one percentage point

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in infancy (ages 0-1), has no statistically significant effect on test taking, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (children whose family post-tax income two years before the real or placebo job loss is BELOW the median).

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in infancy (ages 0-1). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 0-1; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to one if the child has at least one recorded grade-nine mark, from either continuous teacher assessment or a formal examination, and zero otherwise. The paper interprets it as a proxy for grade completion; a zero typically indicates grade retention, dropout, or transfer to a non-standard educational track where conventional grading is not applied.

timing.value: Measured at the end of compulsory schooling, grade nine, at age 16.

units.value: proportion of children (0/1 indicator); a coefficient of 0.01 equals one percentage point

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in early childhood (ages 2-5), has no statistically significant effect on test taking, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (children whose family post-tax income two years before the real or placebo job loss is ABOVE the median).

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in early childhood (ages 2-5). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 2-5; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to one if the child has at least one recorded grade-nine mark, from either continuous teacher assessment or a formal examination, and zero otherwise. claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in infancy (ages 0-1), lowers teacher assessment in maths, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (children whose displaced parent is the FATHER, with a recorded grade-nine teacher assessment in mathematics).

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in infancy (ages 0-1). claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in early childhood (ages 2-5), lowers teacher assessment in maths, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (SONS with a recorded grade-nine teacher assessment in mathematics).

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in early childhood (ages 2-5). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 2-5; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Standardised grade-nine continuous teacher assessment in mathematics, conditional on the child having a recorded mark. Grades are standardised to mean zero and unit variance within the corresponding subject-year distribution.

timing.value: Measured at the end of compulsory schooling, grade nine, at age 16.

units.value: standard deviations of the grade distribution within the corresponding subject-year

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in infancy (ages 0-1), lowers teacher assessment in maths, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (children with BELOW-median family post-tax income and a recorded grade-nine teacher assessment in mathematics).

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in infancy (ages 0-1). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 0-1; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in mid childhood (ages 6-11), has no statistically significant effect on teacher assessment in maths, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (children with BELOW-median family post-tax income and a recorded grade-nine teacher assessment in mathematics).

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in mid childhood (ages 6-11). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 6-11; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

definition.value: Standardised grade-nine continuous teacher assessment in mathematics, conditional on the child having a recorded mark. Grades are standardised to mean zero and unit variance within the corresponding subject-year distribution.

units.value: standard deviations of the grade distribution within the corresponding subject-year

Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 0-1; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Standardised grade-nine continuous teacher assessment in mathematics, conditional on the child having a recorded mark. Grades are standardised to mean zero and unit variance within the corresponding subject-year distribution.

units.value: standard deviations of the grade distribution within the corresponding subject-year

claims.statement: Parental job loss caused by a plant closure, experienced in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16), has no statistically significant effect on teacher assessment in maths, relative to matched untreated children and net of the age-invariant treated-control difference measured on children exposed at ages 17-22 (children with ABOVE-median family post-tax income and a recorded grade-nine teacher assessment in mathematics).

register_source.value: Matched employer-employee registry data covering the universe of workers and job spells, 1980-2017, linked to earnings, unemployment and income registers; the paper names no DST register code.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the child's mother or father (but not both) was employed at a private-sector plant that closed, interacted with an indicator that the child's age a(i) in the plant closure year (t*+1) falls in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16). Closures are identified from year-to-year changes in plant owner, industry, municipality and workforce between end-of-November censuses, requiring a reduction of at least three employees and at least 30 percent of the workforce in plants with at least five employees five years earlier; re-employment of a large share of staff at one new plant is not counted as a closure. Control children are untreated children assigned a placebo closure in the same child-age and calendar year cell.

timing.value: Parental plant closure in year t*+1, when the child is aged 12-16; the base year t* is the year before the closure.

register_source.value: Schooling information reported by educational institutions to the Ministry of Education (Danish administrative education registers); the paper names no DST register code or variable name.

definition.value: Standardised grade-nine continuous teacher assessment in mathematics, conditional on the child having a recorded mark. Grades are standardised to mean zero and unit variance within the corresponding subject-year distribution.

timing.value: Measured at the end of compulsory schooling, grade nine, at age 16.

units.value: standard deviations of the grade distribution within the corresponding subject-year

estimand.target_population: Children aged 12-16 in the year their parent's plant closed, whose parent was a private-sector employee aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure — Children whose family post-tax income two years before the real or placebo job loss is above the median
estimand.time_horizon: Outcome measured once, at the end of compulsory schooling (grade nine, age 16); for children exposed in late childhood / adolescence (ages 12-16) this is 0-4 years after the parental job loss.
estimand.formal_query: E[Y | do(parental plant closure at child age in 12-16)] - E[Y | do(no parental plant closure)], for treated children, differenced against the same contrast for children aged 17-22 at closure

population.description: Matched treated-control pairs restricted to children with ABOVE-median family post-tax income and a recorded grade-nine teacher assessment in mathematics; N = 124,612 for this column.
population.ages: 0-22 in the year of the real or placebo plant closure; outcomes measured at age 16
subgroups_defined: childhood stage at parental job loss: infancy (0-1), early childhood (2-5), mid childhood (6-11), late childhood/adolescence (12-16), and the post-school-age reference group (17-22)
gender of the displaced parent (mother / father)
child gender (daughters / sons)
family post-tax income below / above the median two years before job loss
terciles of predicted impacts on family income, parental unemployment, cohabitation and sickness benefits
baseline family assets (median split) and home ownership
displaced parent is the primary vs the secondary earner
population.selection: Children of private-sector employees aged 25-60 with at least three years of tenure at their firm; children exposed to at most one parental plant closure (mother or father, not both); children born by the calendar year of the job loss; treated children matched 1:1 without replacement within cells of birth year, child gender and displaced-parent gender (98% matched, 130,927 pairs).

identification.source_of_variation: Plant closures and major downsizings at private-sector plants in Denmark, 1986-2017 (51,002 events), identified from matched employer-employee registers; the child's age in the closure year determines the childhood stage of exposure, and children aged 17-22 at closure (for whom the shock cannot affect end-of-school outcomes) serve as the within-design reference group.

key_assumptions.assumption: Age-invariant selection into treatment: in the absence of treatment, any systematic difference in end-of-school outcomes between treated and matched control children would have remained constant across children treated at different ages.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Nonparametric age-at-closure estimates from Equation (2) (Figure 1) are statistically indistinguishable from zero for job losses after compulsory school age; F-tests for the joint significance of the post-compulsory coefficients fail to reject (p = 0.49 for test-taking, p = 0.92 for mathematics); no systematic trends in mathematics achievement among control children by age at placebo job loss (Online Appendix Figure D.1).

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion for the reference group: parental plant closure occurring after the child has completed compulsory schooling (ages 17-22) cannot affect end-of-school performance, so that group identifies the selection term rather than a treatment effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the design's central insight; Figure 1 shows coefficients for ages 18-22 indistinguishable from zero.
